already-have.reason: CS-06 is not implemented, not tracked by any GitHub issue, and does not contradict a recorded owner decision, so it stands; but its cost and one evidence line are wrong and its benefit is overstated. No intent field exists on-chain: executeWithOffchainCount / executeBatchWithOffchainCount take only (ownerIndex, newOffchainCount, target, value, data), and a grep for intent/transcript/descriptionHash under contracts/smart-wallet/src returns nothing. The nearest recorded item is the unchecked "On-chain policy decision taken before wallet launch" checkbox in docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:136-139, which names spend caps / timelocks / validUntil, not an intent digest; I found no issue for that checkbox either. The proposal's "pre-launch; no address change constraints beyond re-pinning codehashes" is the main error: the wallet implementation, factory and verifier are already live on Base Mainnet and byte-bound to the Halmos/Lean discharge, the wallet has no upgrade path, and the implementation address is baked into the CREATE2 init-code hash. Changing the execute ABI therefore means a new implementation, a new factory, new firmware-pinned factory/init-code-hash constants, a new wallet address on every chain, a changed 4-byte selector in a wire format CLAUDE.md marks frozen, and a re-run of the whole contract FV chain. That is permitted pre-production (no funds on-chain, parameters renamable) but it is XL and needs an owner decision, not an L spike. The benefit is also narrower than stated: the firmware already renders and signs from one parsed snapshot, and the contract would recompute the digest from the same (target, value, data), so the check only catches a class downgrade (native shape rendered or committed as BLIND) or a firmware/on-chain decoder disagreement. It adds nothing for ERC-7730, Safe, CoW or typed-call routes, which all fall to BLIND‖calldataDigest on-chain, and nothing for off-chain EIP-712/EIP-1271 signing.
already-have.corrections:

Redeploying implementation + factory changes every wallet address, the firmware-pinned PQ_SMART_WALLET_FACTORY / PROXY_INIT_CODE_HASH (proto/src/lib.rs:271,1480), the pinned codehashes, the DeployedBytecodeReproCheck replay, the Halmos 42-rule discharge, the Lean Wallet/{Execute,ValidateUserOp,TxFlow,CreditLedger,Invariants,UpgradeSafety} and Bridge/{Refinement,EntryPoint} models, the Kontrol harnesses, proto frozen-constant tests, aa format-stability tests and the companion fixtures.
2. The claim "no address change constraints beyond re-pinning codehashes" is false: contracts are live on Base Mainnet and the implementation address is in the CREATE2 init-code hash. Invariant #6 (same seed -> same address on every chain) survives only if the redeploy is uniform across chains before launch.
3. Priority P1 -> P2, as a design spike only. Fold it into the existing now-or-never "on-chain policy before wallet launch" decision (vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:136) so the owner takes ONE redeploy decision covering spend caps / timelock / validUntil / intent digest. Do not implement before that decision.
4. The 80%-of-drain-value coverage figure is unsupported. On-chain decoding covers only empty-data ETH and ERC-20 transfer/approve; state honestly that every other route commits BLIND.
5. Evidence line 4 is inaccurate: dispatch.rs:551-566 is a doc comment describing the priority ladder; pick_sign_pages returns Result<Pages, ()> (dispatch.rs:493,529,607), with no discrete intent-class value. The only classifier is ERC-7730-specific (classify_intent_requirement, dispatch.rs:416). A new FI-hardened class output would have to be added to the dispatcher.
6. The threat statement understates existing device-side controls: ERC-7730 double-render with transcript poison (dispatch.rs:52-60,142; pqsigner-erc7730/src/display/mod.rs:296-345), the mandatory native-value page refusal (dispatch.rs:585-591), the single-snapshot parse feeding both render and digest, and the WYSIWYS differential harness (secure/src/display_under_test/wysiwys_dispatch_differential_tests.rs).
7. The batch path needs a per-record digest array; the proposal covers only the single execute.
8. Not checked: I did not read trezor-comparison.md, the parity sweep, or STATUS.md in full for this idea; a grep over docs/ for intent-digest / EIP-719 / the ethresear.ch link returned nothing. No round-1 verify file exists for CS-06.

feasible.reason:
CS-06 does not defend against its stated threat, and its deployment premise is false.

(1) The on-chain check is a tautology over bytes the firmware itself chose. The contract would recompute intentDigest = f(target, value, data) from the same calldata the firmware built (aa/src/userop.rs:148 reconstruct_execute_calldata; secure/src/nsc/cmd_sign_userop.rs:2008). The chain cannot observe what was painted or whether confirm was pressed.

Bypasses:
- Compromised secure image or renderer bug: it computes the same f over its own calldata and the check passes. An LSB-024-class bug (wrong decimals or symbol, clamped array, dropped field) leaves the canonical operands intact, so the digest still matches.
- Fault injection that skips confirm, skips or reorders pages, or skips the scroll-to-end gate: the digest is unaffected.
- Any Safe execTransaction, multiSend, CoW or ERC-7730 call: the "tiny on-chain decoder" classes these as BLIND‖calldataDigest, which is true for any calldata. These are the complex renderers where the bug class actually lives. The check only bites on ETH and ERC-20, the simplest and best-proven renderers.
- Honest firmware cannot commit the class it rendered. A USDC transfer shown through the ERC-7730 route (ladder step 3, secure/src/tx/display/dispatch.rs:551-566) must still commit ERC20_TRANSFER or it reverts. So the committed class has to be re-derived from calldata, which collapses the check to digest == f(calldata).

The only residual catch is a single fault that splits the committed operand struct from the signed calldata on a native shape. That is already covered on device by the dispatcher CFI and final_set_proof (dispatch.rs:331-382; cmd_sign_userop.rs:1811-1830) and the px transcript proof (cmd_sign_userop.rs:1885). The host differential suite secure/src/display_under_test/wysiwys_dispatch_differential_tests.rs:15-40 separately pins the same render-vs-signed-bytes equality.

(2) "No address change constraints beyond re-pinning codehashes" is false.
- The wallet has no upgrade path: _authorizeUpgrade reverts (contracts/verification/lean/SphincsCVerify/Wallet/UpgradeSafety.lean:6-9).
- The factory holds the implementation as an immutable (contracts/smart-wallet/src/PQSmartWalletFactory.sol:36,93,132).
- The ERC-1967 proxy initcode embeds the implementation address (contracts/smart-wallet/lib/solady/src/utils/LibClone.sol:891-912).
- So a changed executeWithOffchainCount means a new implementation address, a new factory address, a new PROXY_INIT_CODE_HASH, a new 4280-byte initCode, and a new CREATE2 address for every wallet.
- Firmware bakes PQ_SMART_WALLET_FACTORY, PROXY_INIT_CODE_HASH and EXECUTE_SELECTOR (proto/src/lib.rs:1480, 1495, 1221).
- Implementation, factory and verifier are already live on Base Mainnet and byte-pinned (contracts/verification/docs/PINNED_CODEHASHES.md:25-31).
- This is a full multi-chain redeploy of wire formats CLAUDE.md marks frozen. It is permitted pre-launch but needs an owner decision.

No pq1 board change is needed; the hardware constraints are not the obstacle.
